dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: So this is your hideout, huh? Nice place.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: It would be even better if there were some elevated areas for defensive purposes... But, I'm guessing you don't have to worry about break-ins.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How do you like it here?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Well... It'll certainly take some getting used to.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: This place is so peaceful, it's almost uncanny. No howling wind, ferocious beasts, crashing waves, bustling crowds... None of that.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: And that constant sense of restlessness inside me... It finally feels calm. It's so... strange.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: No thanks. I don't want to disturb the peace. It's not an easy feeling to come by.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: There's already more than enough conflict and discord in the world. This is a nice escape.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Thank you for bringing me here.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: No, not at all. It's a nice change of pace.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Would you like to have a chat with me?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Sure! There was something I wanted to ask you, actually.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Oh, really? What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: That's Tubby over there, right? Do you know how she stays aloft like that?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: She looks so... well, for lack of a better word, tubby... Yet she somehow manages to keep floating there, without any kind of power source, as far as I can tell...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: If I can figure out how she pulls that off, maybe I can carry even more firepower into the sky.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm guessing it's some kind of adeptal art from Liyue...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: "Adeptal art"? I've heard of those before, but it sounded so... incredible. It's a shame the adepti are said to be so elusive, at least if the stories are anything to go by.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why don't you ask Tubby herself?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Well, I already tried asking her about it.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: ...But she seemed a bit on edge. She said my expression looked like an eagle stalking its prey...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Or a Qucusaur, more like...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: You think so? Hmm... Qucusaurs are similar to birds of prey in many ways.

choices.text: Such as the look in their eyes?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Yeah, actually. Qucusaurs have prominent brow ridges and forward-facing eyes, just like many birds of prey. This helps them protect their eyes during high-speed maneuvers and allows them to lock onto targets from high altitudes.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: At first glance, they do look pretty scary.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: No wonder Tubby was scared...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: *ahem* Well, I'd never treat Tubby as prey... Plus, I'm not actually a Qucusaur.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: I should find an opportunity to clear up this misunderstanding. Although, since I'm one of the parties involved, I probably can't be the peacemaker this time...

choices.text: Why don't you offer her some feather-care products?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Hmm... That's a good idea. Qucusaurs spend a lot of time taking care of their feathers every day.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: I've developed a few feather-care sprays myself, actually. They keep feathers bright, repel insects, and eliminate odors... Maybe Tubby would find them helpful.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Oh, you really seem to know your stuff. My "mom" and I love collecting little ornaments like that. I wonder if Tubby likes shiny things too.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Hmm... judging by the look of the Realm Currency, I'm guessing the answer is yes.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Yeah. Qucusaurs are carnivores too, much like birds of prey. Their hooked beaks and razor-sharp talons aid them in hunting.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: In addition to all the usual small and medium-sized mammals and fish, they occasionally attack smaller birds too...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Anything you want to do?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: I'd like to scout out the terrain from high up in the air to see if there are any weak spots in our defenses.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This place is pretty safe, you know...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: I was only kidding. I just wanted to get a better look at what you've created.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: I'm used to flying so fast that I have to focus all my energy on distant targets or enemies on the ground. I rarely get a chance to stop and admire the scenery itself.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: But I guess I'll get that chance here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sounds like an interesting trip.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Well, "it's about the journey, not the destination"... Isn't that what people say?

choices.text: So, the scenery on this journey...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Well, it goes without saying that you wouldn't normally see things from such a high angle.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Buildings that you're used to seeing up close suddenly look like tiny little boxes, and mountain peaks that you normally see from far below seem an arm's length away...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...Gazing down from up high is an incredible feeling, almost like the vastness of the world has been compressed into the space of a single painting.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Want me to draw you something to stare at?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Oh, you mean like... a massive mural that can only be seen from the sky? Ha, that actually sounds pretty fun.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: There are plenty of cliffside murals near the Flower-Feather Clan, but not many flat, open areas large enough for a giant work of land art.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: What are you planning to draw? Any ideas?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Actually... How about I lend you a hand? It'll go a lot quicker with someone who can fly up and check the progress, don't you think?

choices.text: Is there anything different about it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good morning, Chasca.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Morning. Any plans for today?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good night, Chasca.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Good night. Get some rest, okay? You need to be ready for whatever tomorrow brings.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Ah, this looks like the Flower-Feather Clan... I remember when I first arrived, I didn't think much of it at all.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: My daily routine was pretty much break a few hot air balloons or tear down a stage, then run away before I got caught...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: But somehow... I guess somewhere along the line, I've grown pretty fond of sights like this.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Huh... is that a conference table? It's such a reassuring presence. Once both sides of an argument are willing to sit down and talk, there's a good chance things will finally move forward.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: It can take a lot of work just to get to that stage. Some people are so stubborn, you pretty much have to drag them kicking and screaming to the negotiation table.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: So although this is where people formally reach an agreement, most of the groundwork is usually laid away from the table.
